analyst_changes: B. Riley cut its target from $431 to $385, keeps Neutral (30 Oct).
Needham cut its price target after Wednesday's rally; new figure not given by MarketBeat (29 Oct).

annual.note: share price change by calendar year (Macrotrends; 2026 to 23 Oct)

backbone: Builds optical transceivers and modules for other firms: data centre 51% of sales, telecom networks 31%, cars/industrial 18%.
Four customers are ~58% of sales: Cisco 20%, Nvidia 16%, Nokia 11%, Amazon 11%.
bear: Customer concentration: losing one big customer would hurt badly.
Thin 12% gross margin and almost no free cash flow after capex.
Technology shift (co-packaged optics) could shrink its market.
Analyst averages are stale and still being cut.
bull: Still growing fast: guide is +43% for this quarter.
New merchant transceiver programme ramps from December; Building 10 adds $3-3.5bn of capacity in early 2027.
check: Q1 EPS guide $4.10-4.25 x 4 = ~$16.7, so the run-rate P/E is ~19x, in line with the quoted 17-18x forward. Free cash flow fell from $207m (FY25) to $4m (FY26) as capex absorbed it.
history_notes: Up in 9 of 11 years from 2015 to 2025, but with huge swings inside each year: 2025 ranged $171 to $528.
Past Nvidia-linked scares (Nov 2024, Aug 2025) were followed by new highs as AI networking demand grew.
Results days have been rough lately: both August reports brought sharp falls despite beats.
name: Fabrinet
oneliner: Thailand-based contract manufacturer of optical parts for AI data centres and telecom. Down 58% from its high, the biggest fall in your list.
range_note: Average targets ($651-716) predate the October fall, so no average is drawn. Newest: B. Riley $431 (Hold, 15 Oct), Susquehanna $600 (Buy, 21 Oct).
verdict: Biggest dip, weakest cash flow. A big fall is not the same as cheap. Don't add before the 2 Nov results; add only if Nvidia/datacom sales recover.

why_down.text: Fell 9% when B. Riley turned bearish over Nvidia component unbundling.
Fell on a warning that component shortages would dip datacom sales.
Fell about 19% on results day despite a beat; Nvidia revenue fell 21% in FY26.
Fell 8% on fears co-packaged optics will replace pluggable modules.
Fell 10.7% in the AI sell-off; targets cut to $431 and $600.
